full_judgment:
Abdul Matin Khan Chowdhury, J:—This appeal at the instance of the defendant is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the District Judge, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 266 of 1978 on 28-5-79 dismissing the appeal which was directed against the judgment and decree passed by the Munsif, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Suit No.446 of 1976 on 27-9-78. 

 2. The appeal arises out of a suit for ejectment of a tenant from the suit holding. Plaintiff's case is that the defendant appellant was a tenant under him at a monthly rental of Tk. 60/- per month as per agreement dated 28-12-70. But inspite of the repeated demand the defend-ant did not pay the rent since February 1975, thus she became a defaulter. The plaintiff's further case was that the premise was required by him for his own use and occupation as such he filed the suit for ejectment. He served the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act determining the tenancy with effect from 1st day of June, 1975 which was duly served on 22-5-75 but as the defendant did not vacate the suit room he has filed this suit for eviction. The defendant entered appearance and contested the suit by filing a written statement. According to her the plaintiff used to grant receipts for few months at a time, although she was paying rent regularly. According to the defendant she was not a defaulter, as such she was not liable to be evicted. The learned Munsif found that she was a defaulter and the suit was decreed. 

 3. Being aggrieved the defendant filed an appeal before the District Judge Khulna. The said appeal was dismissed as not maintainable. According to the district Judge no appeal lay against the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif as the suit was an S.C.C. suit but a re-vision lay before this Court. Being aggrieved the defendant filed this second appeal. 

 "In a suit tried in the Small Cause Court file or in a suit of the nature of a Small Cause Court suit the power of revision is given only to the High Court and not to any subordinate Court. Therefore the court of appeal below could not have heard an appeal against such a judgment nor could he treat it as a revision before him and hence the judgment and decree passed by him must be set aside as being without jurisdiction".
